claims.text: The initial feedstock is gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder without secondary dispersoids.
A minor nanoscale Y2O3 addition on the order of 0.5–2 wt% will be introduced into the AlCrFeNiSi powder before printing.
Nanoscale Y2O3 can be incorporated into metallic powder feedstock for additive manufacturing.
Y2O3 modification will mitigate residual thermal stresses in selectively laser-melted AlCrFeNiSi.
Y2O3 modification will improve the mechanical performance of selectively laser-melted AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed geometry is a miniature component such as a 10 mm cube.
The components will be manufactured by selective laser melting within a low-thermal-load processing window.
Laser power, scan strategy, and layer thickness will be held constant between trials.
The Y2O3 particles will be uniformly dispersed in the printed material.
Y2O3 particles act as heterogeneous nucleation sites during rapid solidification.
Y2O3 dispersoids inhibit grain growth and refine the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Y2O3 modification produces a more homogeneous matrix containing distributed stress-relief sites.
Grain refinement caused by Y2O3 reduces localized thermal gradients that would otherwise generate residual stress.
Y2O3 dispersoids enhance mechanical properties through dispersion strengthening.
Relative to unmodified AlCrFeNiSi made under conventional high-thermal-load conditions, Y2O3-modified components will have lower residual stress.
Relative to that baseline, Y2O3-modified components will have higher tensile strength and ductility.
Relative to that baseline, Y2O3-modified components will have a more uniform microstructure.
The benefits occur only within a narrow window of Y2O3 concentration and laser-processing parameters, and deviations may eliminate the stress-mitigation effect.

contradictions.description: The predicted comparison and baseline use conventional high-thermal-load processing, but the falsification experiment processes both modified and unmodified samples under matched low-thermal-load conditions. It therefore does not directly test the stated comparison against a high-thermal-load baseline.

The conditions state that laser parameters are kept constant between trials, whereas the named baseline is produced under a different high-thermal-load regime. It is unclear whether parameters are matched or intentionally different.
